title: The Voters Both Parties Are Ignoring

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin, and I'm Mark Ronson, and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档关于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you,
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店里做DJ时，你每晚都要带着300件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 然后把DJ台变成一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，陈列着那些精美的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, there are nearly 30 million Latinos in the United States who are eligible to vote, totaling almost 13% of the American electorate.
sentences.zh: 今天，美国有近3000万拉丁裔选民拥有投票权，占美国选民总数的近13%。

sentences.en: So why isn't anyone paying attention to them in the midterms?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么在中期选举中没人关注他们呢？

sentences.en: It's Friday, October 26th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月26日，星期五。

sentences.en: Jose, I want to play this ad for you because I think it's really relevant to what we're going to be talking about today.
sentences.zh: 何塞，我想给你放这段广告，因为我觉得它与我们今天要讨论的话题非常相关。

sentences.en: They're bringing drugs.
sentences.zh: 他们带来了毒品。

sentences.en: They're bringing crime.
sentences.zh: 他们带来了犯罪。

sentences.en: They're rapists.
sentences.zh: 他们是强奸犯。

sentences.en: Can you just describe what's happening here?
sentences.zh: 你能描述一下这里发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: So in this ad, we see a sort of disembodied hand, presumably belonging to President Trump, slapping the faces of several Latino voters.
sentences.zh: 在这则广告中，我们看到一只仿佛没有身体的手，大概属于特朗普总统，正在扇几位拉丁裔选民的耳光。

sentences.en: We have to do something about it, and we have to start by building a wall, a big, beautiful, powerful wall.
sentences.zh: 我们必须采取行动，首先要筑起一堵墙，一堵宏伟、漂亮、坚固的墙。

sentences.en: For the most part, they're just letting him hit them.
sentences.zh: 在大多数情况下，他们只是任由他殴打。

sentences.en: And in the closing scene of this ad, you hear a woman say, in Spanish or in English, depending on the version you're watching.
sentences.zh: 在广告的结尾，你会听到一位女性的声音，根据你观看的版本，可能是西班牙语或英语。

sentences.en: How much longer are we going to endure so many trompadas?
sentences.zh: 我们还要忍受多少次这样的“耳光”？

sentences.en: In Spanish, it's a pun off of the word trompada, which means to punch.
sentences.zh: 在西班牙语中，这是一个关于“trompada”一词的双关语，意思是拳打。

sentences.en: Enough.
sentences.zh: 够了。

sentences.en: Use your power.
sentences.zh: 运用你的力量。

sentences.en: Use your votes.
sentences.zh: 投出你的选票。

sentences.en: Vote for candidates who can stop them.
sentences.zh: 投票给能阻止他们的人。

sentences.en: It's a call to arms in a real way.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上是一种战斗号召。

sentences.en: And in a very sort of literal way, they are saying, you know, we're done getting smacked around by this guy.
sentences.zh: 从字面上看，他们是在说，我们受够了被这家伙欺负。

sentences.en: Jose Del Real is a national reporter for The Times.
sentences.zh: 何塞·德尔·雷亚尔是《纽约时报》的全国记者。

sentences.en: This was paid for by an organization called Mi Familia Vota.
sentences.zh: 这则广告是由一个名为“我的家庭投票”（Mi Familia Vota）的组织出资制作的。

sentences.en: They are a non-profit.
sentences.zh: 他们是一个非营利组织。

sentences.en: They're a national organization.
sentences.zh: 他们是一个全国性组织。

sentences.en: But they're not really in the business of, you know, cutting ads like this.
sentences.zh: 但他们通常并不从事制作这类广告的业务。

sentences.en: What is unique about this situation, and when I talked to them, the reason that they felt they needed to make this intervention,
sentences.zh: 这种情况的独特之处在于，当我与他们交谈时，他们之所以觉得必须进行这种干预，

sentences.en: is they and others truly feel like the Hispanic electorate is not being targeted by campaigns, is not being, you know, contacted.
sentences.zh: 是因为他们和其他人确实感到西班牙裔选民没有受到竞选活动的重视，也没有被联系过。

sentences.en: And so this really eye-grabbing ad that they've put out is an attempt to mobilize Latinos when nobody else has been trying to get them to turn out.
sentences.zh: 所以他们发布的这则引人注目的广告，是试图在没人动员拉丁裔选民投票的情况下，去激励他们。

sentences.en: That's surprising because it seems like the Latino vote would be hugely important for the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 这很令人惊讶，因为拉丁裔的选票对民主党来说似乎非常重要。

sentences.en: Is that generally true?
sentences.zh: 通常情况是这样吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: I mean, if you zoom out today, there are nearly 60 million Hispanics in the United States, and 29 million of those are eligible to vote this year.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果放眼今天，美国有近6000万西班牙裔人口，其中2900万人今年有资格投票。

sentences.en: They are particularly important in terms of a voting bloc for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 对于民主党来说，他们是一个特别重要的选民群体。

sentences.en: And so what is so shocking is to see statistics, like from a tracking poll that Latino Decisions released,
sentences.zh: 所以最令人震惊的是看到一些统计数据，比如“拉丁裔决策”发布的追踪民调显示，

sentences.en: showing that 60% of Hispanics nationally have not been contacted by any campaigns.
sentences.zh: 全国60%的西班牙裔选民没有收到任何竞选活动的联系。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So why then, if this is such a significant voting bloc, would the Democratic Party itself not put out ads like this?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果这是一个如此重要的选民群体，为什么民主党自己不投放这样的广告呢？

sentences.en: Why is this outside group feeling like it has to take matters into its own hands for the midterms?
sentences.zh: 为什么这个外部团体觉得在中期选举中必须亲力亲为？

sentences.en: This is a debate that has been waged within the Democratic Party for years.
sentences.zh: 这是民主党内部多年来一直争论不休的话题。

sentences.en: Two men, one stage, 47 days to go.
sentences.zh: 两人对垒，一个舞台，距离选举还有47天。

sentences.en: You have to go back to the 2012 election.
sentences.zh: 你得回溯到2012年的选举。

sentences.en: This was an election where President Obama was running for re-election, and his opponent, Governor Mitt Romney of Massachusetts,
sentences.zh: 那次选举中，奥巴马总统竞选连任，而他的对手，马萨诸塞州州长米特·罗姆尼，

sentences.en: was, you know, trying to figure out a way to come up against an incumbent who was hugely popular among young voters, among minority voters,
sentences.zh: 正试图想办法对抗一位在年轻选民和少数族裔选民中极受欢迎的在任总统，

sentences.en: you know, what we've come to think of as the Obama coalition.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们所说的“奥巴马联盟”。

sentences.en: Your father was born in Mexico, so the question is, are you Mexican-American?
sentences.zh: 你父亲出生在墨西哥，所以问题是，你是墨西哥裔美国人吗？

sentences.en: Could you be the first Hispanic president?
sentences.zh: 你可能成为第一位西班牙裔总统吗？

sentences.en: I would love to be able to convince people of that, particularly in a Florida primary.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意让人们相信这一点，特别是在佛罗里达州的初选中。

sentences.en: But I think that might be disingenuous on my part because...
sentences.zh: 但我认为那样做可能不够真诚，因为……

sentences.en: What the Republican Party during 2012 was wrestling with was how to mobilize some of its messaging
sentences.zh: 共和党在2012年期间一直在努力解决的问题是如何调整其信息传递策略，

sentences.en: around social conservative issues, around faith, around, you know, small business regulations.
sentences.zh: 围绕社会保守议题、信仰以及小企业监管等方面。

sentences.en: Romney's youngest son, Craig, spoke to a group of Hispanic small business owners.
sentences.zh: 罗姆尼最小的儿子克雷格向一群西班牙裔小企业主发表了讲话。

sentences.en: On some of these topics that Hispanic voters tend to have in common with conservative voters.
sentences.zh: 谈论了一些西班牙裔选民往往与保守派选民有共同点的议题。

sentences.en: Who shares your values?
sentences.zh: 谁与你有共同的价值观？

sentences.en: President Obama used his health care plan to declare war on religion.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马总统利用他的医疗保健计划向宗教宣战。

sentences.en: At the same exact time.
sentences.zh: 就在同一时间。

sentences.en: The president has been feverishly focused on winning Latino voters.
sentences.zh: 总统一直狂热地专注于争取拉丁裔选民。

sentences.en: In Spanish language ads about Supreme Court Justice Sonia Sotomayor.
sentences.zh: 通过关于最高法院大法官索尼娅·索托马约尔的西班牙语广告。

sentences.en: The Democrats and President Obama's campaign, they were reaching out to Latino voters in very targeted ways.
sentences.zh: 民主党和奥巴马总统的竞选团队，他们以非常有针对性的方式接触拉丁裔选民。

sentences.en: The stories of the Latino community are stories about the American dream.
sentences.zh: 拉丁裔社区的故事就是关于美国梦的故事。

sentences.en: Young people who believe that anything is possible.
sentences.zh: 年轻人相信一切皆有可能。

sentences.en: And parents and grandparents working hard to give their children the chance to succeed.
sentences.zh: 父母和祖父母努力工作，给孩子们成功的机会。

sentences.en: And then in August of 2012...
sentences.zh: 然后在2012年8月……

sentences.en: Effective immediately.
sentences.zh: 即刻生效。

sentences.en: Right before the election, you have the introduction of DACA.
sentences.zh: 就在选举前夕，你迎来了“童年抵美者暂缓遣返”（DACA）政策的推出。

sentences.en: The Department of Homeland Security is taking steps to lift the shadow of deportation from these young people.
sentences.zh: 国土安全部正在采取措施，消除这些年轻人被驱逐出境的阴影。

sentences.en: Which really was a huge moment of elation for Hispanic voters and for Latinos broadly who cared about immigration reform.
sentences.zh: 这对西班牙裔选民以及关心移民改革的广大拉丁裔来说，确实是一个令人欢欣鼓舞的时刻。

sentences.en: So how did these dueling strategies, Obama's and Romney's, work out for each of the candidates when it came to the Latino vote?
sentences.zh: 那么，奥巴马和罗姆尼这两种截然不同的策略，在拉丁裔选票方面对各自的候选人效果如何？

sentences.en: Well, I think to answer that question, you really just have to look at the results.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为要回答这个问题，你只需要看看结果。

sentences.en: President Obama won the Hispanic vote by something like 71%.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马总统赢得了约71%的西班牙裔选票。

sentences.en: And Mitt Romney took just 27%.
sentences.zh: 而米特·罗姆尼只拿到了27%。

sentences.en: One of the all-time lows in presidential election history.
sentences.zh: 这是总统选举史上最低的得票率之一。

sentences.en: And what lesson do Republicans take from what looks to be an electoral blowout when it comes to Latino voters?
sentences.zh: 共和党人从这场看似在拉丁裔选民方面的惨败中吸取了什么教训？

sentences.en: We're a little bit too math-focused and not focused in people's hearts.
sentences.zh: 我们太关注数据，而没有关注人们的内心。

sentences.en: So that we don't relate to, I think, average Americans more than we should.
sentences.zh: 以至于我们与普通美国人的共鸣不够。

sentences.en: Stuffy old guys.
sentences.zh: 古板的老家伙们。

sentences.en: They came out in 2012 with the now famous autopsy report, which really instructed candidates to find ways to communicate with Hispanic voters and with other minority voters.
sentences.zh: 他们在2012年发布了现在著名的“尸检报告”，该报告真正指导候选人寻找与西班牙裔选民及其他少数族裔选民沟通的方式。

sentences.en: To bring them out to the polls to show them that the Republican Party is not just open to them, but supports policies that will help them.
sentences.zh: 让他们出来投票，向他们展示共和党不仅对他们开放，而且支持有助于他们的政策。

sentences.en: The report recommends the GOP spend $10 million toward new minority outreach efforts and even more on technology and building an improved voter database.
sentences.zh: 该报告建议共和党投入1000万美元用于新的少数族裔外联工作，并在技术和建立改进的选民数据库上投入更多资金。

sentences.en: An important piece of context that we need to remember is that President George W.
sentences.zh: 我们需要记住的一个重要背景是，乔治·W·布什总统，

sentences.en: Bush was actually fairly popular among Hispanics.
sentences.zh: 实际上在西班牙裔中相当受欢迎。

sentences.en: He pulled in 40% of the Hispanic vote in 2004, just a few elections before.
sentences.zh: 他在2004年，也就是几届选举前，赢得了40%的西班牙裔选票。

sentences.en: That is a huge swing.
sentences.zh: 那是一个巨大的波动。

sentences.en: And what it signaled to strategists in 2012 was that if only they could get the messaging right,
sentences.zh: 这向2012年的战略家们发出的信号是，如果他们能把信息传达正确，

sentences.en: if only they could show Hispanics that Republican conservative policies were going to help improve their lives, then, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果他们能向西班牙裔展示共和党的保守政策将有助于改善他们的生活，那么，

sentences.en: in the future they could wear away at the sort of Democratic Obama coalition that had cost them two presidential elections already.
sentences.zh: 未来他们就能瓦解那种已经让他们输掉两次总统选举的民主党奥巴马联盟。

sentences.en: So once Republicans see that there are potential inroads, what do they actually do to try to win Latino voters back?
sentences.zh: 那么，一旦共和党人看到有潜在的突破口，他们实际上做了什么来试图赢回拉丁裔选民？

sentences.en: So after the 2012 election, after this autopsy report, you have, you know, Jeb Bush, George W.
sentences.zh: 所以在2012年选举之后，在那份尸检报告之后，你有了杰布·布什，当然，他是乔治·W·布什的弟弟，

sentences.en: Bush's brother, of course, running for office, showcasing his bicultural family.
sentences.zh: 他竞选公职时展示了他双文化的家庭。

sentences.en: I'm married to a Mexican-American, United States citizen.
sentences.zh: 我娶了一位墨西哥裔美国人，她是美国公民。

sentences.en: I'm immersed in the culture.
sentences.zh: 我沉浸在这种文化中。

sentences.en: I'm bilingual.
sentences.zh: 我是双语者。

sentences.en: I feel like I'm bicultural.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我是双文化的。

sentences.en: I'm proud of the diversity of my own family.
sentences.zh: 我为自己家庭的多样性感到自豪。

sentences.en: Speaking Spanish at a lot of campaign stops.
sentences.zh: 在许多竞选活动中用西班牙语演讲。

sentences.en: La mayoría eran hispanos.
sentences.zh: 大多数人是西班牙裔。

sentences.en: Mi hijo, George, pues tiene un piel, es moreno, no?
sentences.zh: 我的儿子乔治，他的皮肤是深色的，不是吗？

sentences.en: You have Marco Rubio running on the strength of his support in Florida and on the fact that he had, you know, tried to cooperate on a comprehensive immigration reform bill.
sentences.zh: 你还有马可·卢比奥，他凭借在佛罗里达州的支持率，以及他曾试图在全面移民改革法案上进行合作的事实进行竞选。

sentences.en: And when we talk about illegal immigration, it's not about demanding rights.
sentences.zh: 当我们谈论非法移民时，这不是关于要求权利。

sentences.en: It's about appealing to the compassion of the most compassionate nation in the history of the world.
sentences.zh: 这是关于诉诸世界上最富有同情心的国家的同情心。

sentences.en: You have even Ted Cruz, senator of Texas, at times attempting to speak Spanish at debate.
sentences.zh: 你甚至还有德克萨斯州参议员泰德·克鲁兹，有时在辩论中尝试说西班牙语。

sentences.en: Well, first of all, I don't know how he knows what I said on Univision because he doesn't speak Spanish.
sentences.zh: 首先，我不知道他是怎么知道我在Univision上说了什么的，因为他不会说西班牙语。

sentences.en: And second of all, the other point that I would make—
sentences.zh: 其次，我要提出的另一点是——

sentences.en: Marco, si quiere, díselo ahora mismo, díselo ahora.
sentences.zh: 马可，如果你想的话，现在就说出来，现在就说。

sentences.en: En español, si quiere.
sentences.zh: 用西班牙语，如果你想的话。

sentences.en: And so you really start to see that the Republicans are taking seriously the idea that they need to reach out to Hispanic voters, really trying to meet them where they are.
sentences.zh: 所以你真的开始看到共和党人正在认真对待他们需要接触西班牙裔选民的想法，真正试图在他们所在的地方与他们会面。

sentences.en: Right, and what could be a greater testament to this kind of cultural change within the party than the fact that two of those candidates you just mentioned, Cruz and Rubio,
sentences.zh: 没错，还有什么比你刚才提到的那两位候选人——克鲁兹和卢比奥——本身就是拉丁裔，更能证明党内这种文化变革呢？

sentences.en: are themselves Latino?
sentences.zh: 这超越了政治上的迎合。

sentences.en: It goes beyond political pandering.
sentences.zh: 这是真正的代表性。

sentences.en: It's true representation.
sentences.zh: 让杰布·布什的双文化家庭在新闻中显眼地出现，让他吹嘘自己流利说西班牙语的能力，

sentences.en: To have Jeb Bush's bicultural family prominently featured on the news, to have him bragging about his ability to speak Spanish fluently,
sentences.zh: 这向西班牙裔选民发出了非常积极的包容和支持信号。

sentences.en: that sends really positive signals of inclusivity and of support to Hispanic voters.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为这一点怎么强调都不为过。

sentences.en: And I really think that that can't be overstated.
sentences.zh: 然后唐纳德·特朗普出现了。

sentences.en: And then came Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 当墨西哥送他们的人来时，他们送来的不是最好的人。

sentences.en: When Mexico sends its people, they're not sending their beSt.
sentences.zh: 他们送来的不是你。

sentences.en: They're not sending you.
sentences.zh: 他们送来的不是你。

sentences.en: They're not sending you.
sentences.zh: 他们送来的是有很多问题的人，他们把这些问题带给了我们。

sentences.en: They're sending people that have lots of problems, and they're bringing those problems with us.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的是特朗普主义，特别是特朗普与移民相关的争议性言论，慢慢渗透到共和党的主流中。

sentences.en: What we see is Trumpism, and in particular Trump's controversial immigration-related rhetoric, slowly creep into the mainstream of the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 在那次竞选期间。

sentences.en: During that campaign.
sentences.zh: 在那次竞选期间。

sentences.en: During that campaign.
sentences.zh: 但在2015年，当他首次宣布参选时，我认为共和党人对他的言论感到震惊，并试图找出如何边缘化他，

sentences.en: But in 2015, when he first announced his candidacy, I think that Republicans were aghast at his remarks and were trying to figure out how to marginalize him,
sentences.zh: 但没想到他会成为他们党的提名人，并最终成为总统。

sentences.en: but did not imagine that he would become the nominee for their party and eventually the president.
sentences.zh: 现在，我想我在西班牙裔中会表现得很好。

sentences.en: Now, I think I'm going to do very well with Hispanics.
sentences.zh: 你知道为什么我在西班牙裔中会表现得很好吗？

sentences.en: You know why I'm going to do well with Hispanics?
sentences.zh: 因为我要带回就业机会，他们现在就能得到工作。

sentences.en: Because I'm going to bring back jobs, and they're going to get jobs right now.
sentences.zh: 他们会得到工作。

sentences.en: They're going to get jobs.
sentences.zh: 我想我在西班牙裔中会表现得很好。

sentences.en: I think I'm going to do very well with Hispanics.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显我们知道2016年的选举结果如何，但那次选举中拉丁裔的选票到底是如何分布的？

sentences.en: So obviously we know how the election turned out in 2016, but how exactly did the Latino vote shake out in that election?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是令人震惊的地方。

sentences.en: Well, this is where there was a bit of a shock.
sentences.zh: 当时的出口民调显示，在2016年选举中，约有30%的西班牙裔选民实际上支持特朗普总统。

sentences.en: Exit polls at the time showed that around 30% of Hispanic voters actually supported President Trump during the 2016 election.
sentences.zh: 他在投票箱的表现实际上比米特·罗姆尼还要好一点。

sentences.en: He actually did a little bit better than Mitt Romney did at the ballot box.
sentences.zh: 比罗姆尼好。

sentences.en: Better than Romney.
sentences.zh: 比罗姆尼好。

sentences.en: Better than Romney.
sentences.zh: 这感觉确实出人意料。

sentences.en: That feels genuinely unexpected.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我看到出口民调时，是的，我的第一反应是惊讶。

sentences.en: You know, when I saw the exit polls, yeah, my first instinct was surprise.
sentences.zh: 我以为他得到的选民会比罗姆尼在2012年少得多。

sentences.en: I thought that he would get a lot fewer voters than Romney did in 2012.
sentences.zh: 但当我开始查看数据时，

sentences.en: But then when I started looking at the numbers as they became available,
sentences.zh: 我意识到，倾向共和党的拉丁裔选民以与以往竞选活动相同的比例出现，这并不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: my realization was that it wasn't so surprising that Republican-leaning Latinos showed up at the same rate that they did in previous campaigns.
sentences.zh: 令我惊讶的是，创纪录数量的拉丁裔选民没有投票。

sentences.en: What was surprising to me is that a record number of Latinos didn't vote.
sentences.zh: 1430万西班牙裔选民在2016年没有投票。

sentences.en: 14.3 million Hispanic voters did not cast ballots in 2016.
sentences.zh: 尽管这场竞选在理论上似乎非常能激励拉丁裔选民反对唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: Despite a race that seemed like it would very much animate Latino voters theoretically against Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 这向我表明了什么，而且我认为自那以后我在全国各地的谈话中也得到了证实，

sentences.en: And what that indicated to me, and what I think has been borne out in conversations I've had across the country since then,
sentences.zh: 那就是仅靠特朗普一个人不足以激励许多选民。

sentences.en: is that Trump alone was not enough to motivate a lot of voters.
sentences.zh: 仅靠移民政策不足以激励其中一些选民。

sentences.en: Immigration policy alone was not enough to motivate some of these voters.
sentences.zh: 仅靠移民政策不足以激励其中一些选民。

sentences.en: What I concluded, and I think what a lot of other people are starting to see, is that the Latino vote is just much more complicated, much more nuanced than we understood before.
sentences.zh: 我的结论是——我想很多人也开始意识到了——拉丁裔选民的投票意向远比我们之前理解的要复杂得多，也微妙得多。

sentences.en: And they care about a lot more issues than they are being spoken to about.
sentences.zh: 而且他们关心的议题远比政客们跟他们谈论的要多。

sentences.en: I'm from the New York Times, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我来自《纽约时报》，没错。

sentences.en: I actually am based in L.A.
sentences.zh: 我其实常驻洛杉矶。

sentences.en: I'm a correspondent, and we have euros all over the country.
sentences.zh: 我是一名记者，我们在全国各地都有驻点。

sentences.en: So, not too long of a trek here.
sentences.zh: 所以，到这儿来不算太远。

sentences.en: So, what does 2016 tell us about the Latino vote that we didn't understand before?
sentences.zh: 那么，2016年的大选向我们揭示了哪些我们之前没能理解的拉丁裔选民投票倾向？

sentences.en: If a Republican presidential candidate being so openly anti-immigration doesn't turn the Latino vote out, what does that mean in 2018?
sentences.zh: 如果一位共和党总统候选人如此公开地反移民都无法激发拉丁裔选民的投票热情，那这在2018年意味着什么？

sentences.en: You know, that question, as we're heading into the midterm election, was really tantalizing to me.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在我们走向中期选举时，这个问题真的让我非常着迷。

sentences.en: So, I decided to just go to Nevada, where there is a competitive Senate race.
sentences.zh: 所以，我决定直接去内华达州，那里有一场竞争激烈的参议院席位争夺战。

sentences.en: And according to political strategists, the difference between, you know, 15% of Latinos showing up and 17% of Latinos showing up could flip the race.
sentences.zh: 据政治策略师分析，你知道，15%的拉丁裔投票率和17%的投票率之间的差距，就足以扭转选情。

sentences.en: Sandra?
sentences.zh: 桑德拉？

sentences.en: Is your apellido Sandra?
sentences.zh: 你的姓是桑德拉吗？

sentences.en: I keep thinking to a woman named Sandra Alvaro, who I met outside of a store called Cardenas.
sentences.zh: 我一直想起一位叫桑德拉·阿尔瓦罗的女士，我是在一家叫卡德纳斯的商店外遇到她的。

sentences.en: It's a Hispanic market in Las Vegas.
sentences.zh: 那是拉斯维加斯的一家西班牙裔市场。

sentences.en: And Ms. Alvaro was telling me, you know, I have voted every election for years and years and years.
sentences.zh: 阿尔瓦罗女士当时告诉我，你知道，多年来我每次选举都去投票。

sentences.en: And nothing changes for me or my community.
sentences.zh: 但对我或我的社区来说，什么都没有改变。

sentences.en: She said, I care about mental health issues.
sentences.zh: 她说，我关心心理健康问题。

sentences.en: I care about education for my kids.
sentences.zh: 我关心我孩子受教育的问题。

sentences.en: I care about how much money we're able to bring home.
sentences.zh: 我关心我们能带回家多少钱。

sentences.en: And it just feels like every two to four years, we hear these candidates come out and talk about how they're going to help us.
sentences.zh: 感觉每隔两到四年，我们就会听到这些候选人出来说他们会如何帮助我们。

sentences.en: And then the election passes and they forget about us.
sentences.zh: 然后选举一过，他们就把我们忘了。

sentences.en: And she said, I'm basically nonpartisan at this point because I just don't see the point.
sentences.zh: 她说，我现在基本上不站队了，因为我根本看不出投票的意义。

sentences.en: There was another man I spoke to, Enrique González.
sentences.zh: 我还和另一位男士谈过，恩里克·冈萨雷斯。

sentences.en: He's 50 years old.
sentences.zh: 他今年50岁。

sentences.en: I met him at that same grocery store in Las Vegas.
sentences.zh: 我是在拉斯维加斯同一家杂货店遇到他的。

sentences.en: And he had a whole different view of this.
sentences.zh: 他对这件事有完全不同的看法。

sentences.en: He became a citizen six years ago.
sentences.zh: 他六年前成为了公民。

sentences.en: He said he hasn't missed an election since then.
sentences.zh: 他说从那以后他从未错过任何一次选举。

sentences.en: He had a big smile on his face when I asked him about what it meant to him to vote.
sentences.zh: 当我问他投票对他意味着什么时，他脸上露出了灿烂的笑容。

sentences.en: And he told me that a lot of his friends don't vote because...
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，他的很多朋友不去投票是因为……

sentences.en: A lot of the people that he speaks to in his community have a feeling that the elections themselves, like elections in some Latin American countries and in Mexico,
sentences.zh: 他在社区里交谈过的许多人都有种感觉，认为选举本身，就像一些拉美国家和墨西哥的选举一样，

sentences.en: are sort of rigged, are stacked against the will of the people anyway.
sentences.zh: 某种程度上是被操纵的，无论如何都是违背人民意愿的。

sentences.en: And the issue of immigration, just from having conversations with people, is itself quite divisive.
sentences.zh: 而且移民问题，仅仅从与人们的交谈来看，本身就相当具有分裂性。

sentences.en: And people feel differently about it based on their own recent ancestry, based on whether they have recent family members who are immigrants,
sentences.zh: 人们对它的看法各不相同，这取决于他们自己的近期祖籍，取决于他们是否有近亲是移民，

sentences.en: or whether they've been here for generations, their income, their age.
sentences.zh: 或者他们是否已经在当地生活了几代人，以及他们的收入和年龄。

sentences.en: People talk about Trump, they're like, oh, he's a raciSt.
sentences.zh: 人们谈论特朗普时会说，哦，他是个种族主义者。

sentences.en: Like, come on, the only people that he deported are gang members.
sentences.zh: 得了吧，他驱逐的唯一群体就是帮派成员。

sentences.en: The majority of the people that deported are gang members, and they're here for trafficking and drugs.
sentences.zh: 被驱逐的人中大多数是帮派成员，他们在这里是为了贩运人口和毒品。

sentences.en: That's one thing we need less in our community as in our state.
sentences.zh: 那是我们社区乃至我们州需要减少的东西。

sentences.en: I had a conversation with a young man named Jose Alvarez.
sentences.zh: 我和一位叫何塞·阿尔瓦雷斯的年轻人谈过话。

sentences.en: He's 20 years old.
sentences.zh: 他今年20岁。

sentences.en: And I just asked him, you know, are you going to vote?
sentences.zh: 我只是问他，你知道，你会去投票吗？

sentences.en: Are you following the election?
sentences.zh: 你有在关注这次选举吗？

sentences.en: I sort of expected, you know, this is a young Mexican guy, I sort of expected that he would either sigh, which is what many people do, or start talking about how offensive he was.
sentences.zh: 我本来预想，你知道，这是一个年轻的墨西哥小伙子，我预想他要么会叹气——这是许多人的反应，要么会开始谈论他有多么令人反感。

sentences.en: But in fact, he actually supports President Trump's deportation policies.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，他其实支持特朗普总统的驱逐政策。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Well, I'm a Republican.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我是共和党人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I like Republicans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢共和党人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I like Trump.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢特朗普。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I think he's a great president.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他是一位伟大的总统。

sentences.en: I think he made our economy much better.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他让我们的经济好多了。

sentences.en: Yes, he might be a little reckless.
sentences.zh: 是的，他可能有点鲁莽。

sentences.en: He might act like a little kid sometimes.
sentences.zh: 他有时可能表现得像个小孩子。

sentences.en: But our work has been booming off charts.
sentences.zh: 但我们的工作一直非常火爆。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: He's been building all kinds of work for us all around the country, you know?
sentences.zh: 他一直在为我们全国各地创造各种工作机会，你知道吗？

sentences.en: He works in masonry.
sentences.zh: 他从事泥瓦匠工作。

sentences.en: He feels like Trump's economic policies and his immigration policies were making things better for him, and in that order.
sentences.zh: 他觉得特朗普的经济政策和移民政策让他的生活变得更好，而且是按这个顺序。

sentences.en: So how does that complicated diversity that you have found influence how Democrats and Republicans are trying to win Latino votes in this upcoming midterm?
sentences.zh: 那么，你所发现的这种复杂的多元性，如何影响民主党和共和党在即将到来的中期选举中争取拉丁裔选票的策略？

sentences.en: I think that the truth is that despite everything we saw in the 2016 election, despite the 2012 autopsy report, despite George W.
sentences.zh: 我认为事实是，尽管我们在2016年大选中看到了这一切，尽管有2012年的选后分析报告，尽管乔治·W·布什在西班牙裔选民中取得了相对成功，

sentences.en: Bush's relative success with Hispanic voters, there is a feeling and a conventional wisdom that the only way to speak to Hispanics is with regards to immigration issues.
sentences.zh: 但人们依然有一种感觉和传统观念，认为与西班牙裔沟通的唯一方式就是谈论移民问题。

sentences.en: And I think that impulse to see this voting bloc as absolutely monolithic is part of what has led to this ingrained political apathy.
sentences.zh: 我认为将这个投票群体视为绝对同质化的冲动，正是导致这种根深蒂固的政治冷漠的原因之一。

sentences.en: So because both parties have for so long struggled, maybe even failed to understand, that Latinos are not monolithic,
sentences.zh: 所以，正因为两党长期以来都在挣扎，甚至未能理解拉丁裔并非铁板一块，

sentences.en: that there are a variety of interests and issues and passions in this electorate,
sentences.zh: 这个选民群体有着各种各样的利益、议题和热情，

sentences.en: that they are both still talking to them as if they were a monolith, and that it's that blind spot inside both parties that further alienates Latino voters.
sentences.zh: 而他们依然像对待一个同质化群体那样与他们对话，正是两党内部的这种盲点，进一步疏远了拉丁裔选民。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Around 60 percent of registered Latino voters nationwide are not even being contacted by these campaigns.
sentences.zh: 全国约60%的注册拉丁裔选民甚至没有收到这些竞选团队的联络。

sentences.en: And when they are, it's largely focused on President Trump and his comments, which didn't motivate them to turn out in 2016,
sentences.zh: 而当他们收到联络时，内容主要集中在特朗普总统及其言论上，这并没有激励他们在2016年出来投票，

sentences.en: and about immigration policy, which we've been hearing about for decades.
sentences.zh: 以及关于我们几十年来一直听到的移民政策。

sentences.en: How much longer are we going to endure so many trompadas enough?
sentences.zh: 我们还要忍受多少次这样的打击才够？

sentences.en: And that kind of brings us back to that ad we started our conversation talking about.
sentences.zh: 这又把我们带回了我们谈话开始时提到的那则广告。

sentences.en: This outside group, this Latino group, very much worried that Hispanic voters are being ignored by both parties,
sentences.zh: 这个外部团体，这个拉丁裔团体，非常担心西班牙裔选民被两党忽视，

sentences.en: but especially the Democrats, decides to take matters into its own hands.
sentences.zh: 尤其是被民主党忽视，于是决定采取行动。

sentences.en: But in doing so, in creating this ad, focuses on this one issue, immigration, that pretty much ignores this political diversity that you just described.
sentences.zh: 但在这样做时，在制作这则广告时，它只关注了移民这一个议题，这几乎忽略了你刚才描述的政治多元性。

sentences.en: So it kind of commits the same sin, in a sense.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，它犯了同样的错误。

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是这样。

sentences.en: And it's also coming out just two weeks before the election.
sentences.zh: 而且它是在选举前两周才发布的。

sentences.en: And so, you know, of course this ad, you know, has shock value to it, which is supposed to grab eyeballs.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，当然这则广告具有冲击力，旨在吸引眼球。

sentences.en: But the truth is that there's only so much that you can do in the last two weeks before an election if, in the run-up to November,
sentences.zh: 但事实是，如果在11月大选前的准备阶段，你没有与这些选民就他们感兴趣的各种议题进行持续的接触，

sentences.en: you haven't made sustained contact with some of these voters about the various issues that they're interested in.
sentences.zh: 那么在选举前的最后两周，你所能做的也就非常有限了。

sentences.en: So I guess, in a sense, because this midterm already feels like a little bit of a wash when it comes to Latino voters,
sentences.zh: 所以我想，从某种意义上说，因为这次中期选举在拉丁裔选民方面已经感觉有点无望了，

sentences.en: it's a question of who gets to them in time for the next presidential election, 2020.
sentences.zh: 问题在于谁能在下一次总统大选（2020年）之前及时争取到他们。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And what we find is a real chicken-and-egg situation when we're trying to figure out how to best approach Latino voters and get them to turn out.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，当我们试图找出接近拉丁裔选民并让他们出来投票的最佳方式时，这是一个真正的“先有鸡还是先有蛋”的问题。

sentences.en: Are they not showing up because nobody's reaching out to them?
sentences.zh: 是因为没人联系他们，所以他们才不出来投票吗？

sentences.en: Or are people not reaching out to them because they're not showing up?
sentences.zh: 还是因为他们不出来投票，所以人们才不去联系他们？

sentences.en: Jose, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 何塞，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Oh, no, thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 哦，不，谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: Times reports that with less than two weeks until the midterms,
sentences.zh: 《时报》报道称，距离中期选举不到两周，

sentences.en: President Trump is considering shutting the southern border to Central American migrants and denying them the chance to seek asylum, using the same powers he invoked in 2017
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统正在考虑关闭南部边境，禁止中美洲移民入境，并拒绝他们寻求庇护的机会，他动用了与2017年针对多数穆斯林国家实施旅行禁令时相同的权力。

sentences.en: to declare a travel ban against mostly Muslim countries.
sentences.zh: 此举将是他为了保住共和党对国会的控制权，而向反移民选民发出的最大胆的呼吁。

sentences.en: The move would be his boldest appeal yet to anti-immigrant voters as he seeks to keep Republican control of Congress.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·罗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档关于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you
sentences.zh: 即使在我还在夜店用黑胶唱片做DJ的年代，你每天都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班，

sentences.en: and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个充满50年历史精美文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th,
I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 我将在纽约市的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、

sentences.en: Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 佐兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无保留、未经剪辑的现场对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日于nytimes.com上直播部分采访内容，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得一个月的免费阅读权限，畅享我们所有的报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On Thursday, federal investigators said that the number of homemade pipe bombs sent to critics of President Trump had grown to 10.
sentences.zh: 周四，联邦调查人员表示，寄给特朗普总统批评者的自制管状炸弹数量已增加到10枚。

sentences.en: We have a president who does not understand governance.
sentences.zh: 我们有一位不懂治理的总统。

sentences.en: Forget his policies for a minute.
sentences.zh: 先别管他的政策。

sentences.en: He doesn't understand how the government functions.
sentences.zh: 他根本不懂政府是如何运作的。

sentences.en: The recipients of the devices now range from former Vice President Joe Biden, a potential rival to Trump in 2020,
sentences.zh: 这些装置的接收者现在包括前副总统乔·拜登，他是特朗普在2020年的潜在竞争对手，

sentences.en: to the actor Robert De Niro, who has repeatedly mocked the president.
sentences.zh: 以及多次嘲讽总统的演员罗伯特·德尼罗。

sentences.en: I mean, he's so blatantly stupid.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他简直蠢得无可救药。

sentences.en: He's a punk.
sentences.zh: 他是个混蛋。

sentences.en: He's a dog.
sentences.zh: 他是个走狗。

sentences.en: He's a pig.
sentences.zh: 他是个猪猡。

sentences.en: It makes me so angry that this country has gotten to this point, that this fool, this bozo, has wound up where he has.
sentences.zh: 这个国家竟然走到了这一步，让这个傻瓜、这个小丑落到今天这个地步，这让我感到非常愤怒。

sentences.en: The Times reports that the bombs have triggered a massive nationwide manhunt that is now focused on southern Florida, where authorities now believe several of the bombs originated.
sentences.zh: 《时报》报道称，这些炸弹引发了一场大规模的全国搜捕行动，目前重点集中在佛罗里达州南部，当局认为几枚炸弹最初就是从那里寄出的。

sentences.en: President Trump, who called for unity after the first bombs were discovered, changed his message on Thursday, pointing the blame at the news media.
sentences.zh: 在发现第一批炸弹后呼吁团结的特朗普总统，在周四改变了口径，将矛头指向了新闻媒体。

sentences.en: In a tweet, the president wrote,
sentences.zh: 总统在推特上写道，

sentences.en: A very big part of the anger we see today in our society is caused by the purposely false and inaccurate reporting of the mainstream media that I refer to as fake news.
sentences.zh: 我们今天在社会中看到的愤怒，很大一部分是由我所称的“假新闻”主流媒体故意发布虚假和不准确的报道所引起的。

sentences.en: It has gotten so bad and hateful, he added, that it is beyond description.
sentences.zh: 他补充说，情况已经变得如此糟糕和充满仇恨，简直无法形容。

sentences.en: Mainstream media must clean up its act faSt.
sentences.zh: 主流媒体必须尽快改过自新。
